question: Bind — ATK, 4v2 up, no spike, 1:05 left. You are pushing B (near B Window) with an Odin and full util, up two players. Only two defenders remain, positions unknown. How do you convert the numbers?

options.label: Play the man-advantage patiently: clear with util and trade-pairs, taking space you can't lose so the 4v2 stays a 4v2
options.explication_courte: Up 4v2, the enemy needs multi-kills to get back in it — so deny them exactly that. Advance in trade pairs, use util to clear angles instead of your body, and never give a defender an isolated 1v1. Numbers win if you don't gift them back.

sources_option.citation: With a man-advantage, take space methodically in trade pairs and use utility to clear; avoid isolated duels that let the enemy even the count

options.label: Spray the Odin through the B Window wall on a common hold to try for a free wallbang pick
options.explication_courte: The Odin's wall penetration can pressure a known hold, but blind-spraying with only two enemies left mostly wastes a huge mag and reveals your position; do it off real info, not on spec, or you're reloading when they peek.

sources_option.citation: Wallbang pressure works off information, not blind spray; an empty mag and a revealed position undoes the advantage

options.label: Rush B fast and loud to overwhelm the two defenders before they can rotate for help
options.explication_courte: There is no help coming — it's 4v2. Rushing loud into two set defenders trades your safety for speed you don't need and can walk your trade-pairs into a double-peek that clips two of you and evens the round.

sources_option.citation: Don't rush when time and numbers favour you; the only way to lose a man-advantage is to hand the enemy quick multi-kills

options.label: Split your four players two-and-two to hit B from two angles at once
options.explication_courte: Splitting a 4v2 into two 2-mans throws away the crushing advantage — you create two even-ish fights where a defender can win a duel and suddenly it's 3v2 or worse. Stack your numbers, don't dilute them.

sources_option.citation: Diluting a numbers advantage into split pushes creates near-even fights; concentrate force to keep the advantage decisive

explication_longue: Up 4v2 with a minute left, the round is yours to lose, and there is exactly one way to lose it: give the two remaining defenders the quick multi-kills they need to climb back into the round. Everything about the correct play flows from that. Pushing B near B Window with an Odin and full util, you advance in trade pairs — two players covering each other so any defender who takes a duel is instantly traded — and you use utility to clear the dangerous angles instead of walking your body into them. That keeps every fight a 2-on-1 in your favour and the count stuck at 4v2. Wallbanging with the Odin is a real tool but only off information; blind-spraying a wall with two enemies left mostly empties a huge magazine and pinpoints you, so you're reloading when they peek. Rushing loud is pointless — no defensive reinforcement is coming in a 4v2 — and it risks a double-peek clipping two of you at once. Worst is splitting two-and-two: that dissolves a crushing advantage into two near-even fights where a single lost duel flips the momentum. Stack the numbers, trade every entry, take space you can't lose.

sources.citation: Convert a man-advantage by taking space in trade pairs with utility; the enemy needs multi-kills, so never give an isolated duel
